title: Mansaf
subtitle: Jordanian lamb with rice and yoghurt sauce
excerpt: Slow-braised bone-in lamb shoulder served over fragrant rice with a rich yoghurt sauce and toasted flaked almonds. Jordan's national dish is a celebration meal that rewards the time it takes.
sourceNotes: Mansaf is the national dish of Jordan and a symbol of Bedouin hospitality, traditionally eaten at weddings, funerals, and family gatherings. It is historically made with jameed, a dried fermented yoghurt from goat or sheep milk. This recipe uses thick Greek yoghurt as a practical substitute.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb can be braised a day ahead and gently reheated. Cook the rice fresh on the day.

content.text: When adding the yoghurt to the hot broth, do so slowly and stir constantly. If the heat is too high or the yoghurt goes in too fast, the sauce will split. Keep the heat low and do not let it boil after the yoghurt is added.

Put the lamb in the stockpot with the stock, onion, garlic, cinnamon, cardamom, allspice, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, skim, then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours until the lamb is very tender and falling off the bone.
Lift the lamb out carefully and set aside. Strain the broth and discard the solids. You need about 800 ml of broth for the rice and sauce.

Cook the rice. Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Drain the soaked rice and add to the pan. Stir for 1 minute. Add 600 ml of the strained broth and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and reduce to the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.

Make the yoghurt sauce. Bring the remaining 200 ml of broth to a very gentle simmer. Whisk the Greek yoghurt in a bowl until smooth. Ladle a little hot broth into the yoghurt while stirring, then slowly pour the warmed yoghurt back into the pan, stirring constantly over low heat. Do not let it boil. Season with salt.
Spread the rice on a large serving platter. Lay the lamb pieces over the rice. Spoon some of the yoghurt sauce over the top and scatter with toasted almonds. Serve the remaining sauce on the side.

items.cause: Added to the broth too fast or over too high heat
items.fix: Use low heat and add yoghurt slowly while stirring.

items.cause: Lid removed too early during resting
items.fix: Leave the rice covered and undisturbed for the full 10 minutes off the heat.

items.cause: Heat was too high or lamb pieces too large
items.fix: Cook for a further 30 minutes on a very low simmer.
